name: V-Bar Lat Pulldown
summary: A seated vertical pulling exercise using a close neutral V-bar attachment to target the latissimus dorsi and upper back.

setup: Attach a V-bar (close-grip triangle handle) to the high pulley of a lat pulldown station.
Adjust the thigh pads so your legs are securely anchored with feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with a neutral grip and sit down, securing your thighs beneath the pads with arms fully extended overhead and chest lifted.
steps: Initiate the pull by depressing and retracting your shoulder blades, leaning back slightly through the hips without hyperextending your lower back.
Drive your elbows down and back, pulling the V-bar toward your upper chest.
Pause briefly at the bottom while contracting your lats.
Slowly reverse the movement, extending your arms and allowing your shoulder blades to elevate to a full stretch at the top.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you pull the handle down to your chest; inhale as you return the weight smoothly to the starting position.
cues: Drive your elbows down to your pockets.
Puff your chest up to meet the handle.
Control the stretch at the top without letting the stack slam.

common_faults.fault: Excessive torso swing and leaning too far back to heave the weight down.
common_faults.correction: Keep your torso relatively fixed with only a slight natural backward lean of about ten to fifteen degrees.

common_faults.fault: Cutting the range of motion short at the top.
common_faults.correction: Allow your arms to fully extend and shoulder blades to elevate for a deep stretch on the lats between repetitions.

common_faults.fault: Pulling primarily with the arms and rolling shoulders forward at the bottom.
common_faults.correction: Lead with scapular depression and focus on driving through the elbows rather than curling with the biceps.

precautions: Ensure the thigh pads are locked firmly over your legs before starting the set.
